Description:
The plainest of the NURBS quadric cases: a cone and a cylinder that share an axis and cut each other in
a single circle. Neither body is a primitive and neither surface is one of CADability's own quadrics -
the cone is a solid.ruled between two exact NURBS circles and comes out as RuledSurface, the cylinder is
a solid.extrude of a third one and comes out as SurfaceOfLinearExtrusion. All three circles are the
classical nine pole rational quadratic form with the corner weights sqrt(2)/2, so they are circles in
the exact sense and not approximations of one.

  nurbsCone   r = 16 at z = 0 shrinking to r = 10 at z = 30, so its radius is 16 - 0.2*z
  nurbsCyl    r = 12 about the z axis, from z = -5 to z = 35

The two mantles meet where 16 - 0.2*z = 12, that is in the single circle r = 12, z = 20, and they meet
TRANSVERSALLY: the cone's surface normal there is tilted by its half angle against the cylinder's, so
the intersection curve is regular and there is NO point of tangential contact anywhere in the case.
That is what it is for. It is the companion of the tangential set (NurbsCylindersTangentAtSeam,
NurbsTorusTangentInnerEquator, NurbsConesTangentAtMantlePoint) on the same kind of surfaces, so that a
failure here can be told apart from a failure of the contact handling - this one would be a failure of
the ordinary intersection path.

The five z levels -5, 0, 20, 30 and 35 are deliberately all different: no cap of one body lies in the
plane of a cap of the other, and no cap meets the intersection circle. Nothing in this case is
degenerate on purpose.
Expected:
Two closed solids and four closed results, every volume exact - the bodies are an exact cone and an
exact cylinder, so nothing here has to be measured.

  nurbsCone   V = pi*30/3*(16^2+16*10+10^2) = 5160*pi = 16210.6180925233
              slant sqrt(30^2+6^2) = sqrt(936) = 30.5941170816
              A = pi*(16+10)*slant + pi*16^2 + pi*10^2 = 3617.3775748066
              extent -16, -16, 0 .. 16, 16, 30
  nurbsCyl    V = pi*12^2*40 = 5760*pi = 18095.5736846772
              A = 2*pi*12*40 + 2*pi*12^2 = 3920.7076316801
              extent -12, -12, -5 .. 12, 12, 35

The intersection is the cylinder below the crossing circle plus the cone above it:
  coneCylInter  pi*12^2*20 + pi*10/3*(12^2+12*10+10^2) = 4093.3333*pi = 12859.5859286942
and everything else follows from it exactly:
  coneCylUnion  (5760 + 5160 - 4093.3333)*pi = 6826.6667*pi = 21446.6058485063
  cylMinusCone  (5760 - 4093.3333)*pi        = 1666.6667*pi =  5235.9877559830
  coneMinusCyl  (5160 - 4093.3333)*pi        = 1066.6667*pi =  3351.0321638291

The SHAPES are pinned as well and are not the same for the two differences:
  cylMinusCone  TWO solids. For 0 <= z <= 20 the cone is wider than the cylinder, so the whole cylinder
                is removed there and the rest falls apart into the disc below the cone,
                pi*144*5 = 2261.9467105847, and the part above the crossing circle,
                pi*144*15 - 1213.3333*pi = 2974.0410453983.
  coneMinusCyl  ONE solid, and a RING: for 0 <= z <= 20 what is left of the cone is the annulus between
                the cylinder and the cone, and the cylinder drills right through it. Euler 0 with a hole
                loop, not Euler 2.
  coneCylInter  one solid, Euler 2.
  coneCylUnion  one solid, Euler 2.

edgeLength carries the second documented measurement defect of NURBS circles: ICurve.Length of a
rational BSpline is the chord polygon through its spans, so a circle measures 4*r*sqrt(2) instead of
2*pi*r - r = 16 gives 90.5096679919, r = 12 gives 67.8822509939, r = 10 gives 56.5685424949. For the two
operands that predicts
  nurbsCone   90.5096679919 + 56.5685424949 + 2*30.5941170816 = 208.2664446500
  nurbsCyl    2*67.8822509939 + 2*40 = 215.7645019878

WHY THESE RADII AND NOT OTHERS - HISTORICAL, THE DEFECT IS FIXED. A planar face whose outline is a
rational NURBS circle used to be measured through Border.Area -> BSpline2D.GetArea ->
GeneralCurve2D.GetArea -> Approximate(false, 0.0), and for most radii that biarc approximation
degenerated into four straight lines, so the lid measured 2*r*r instead of pi*r*r. It was not even a
threshold: exact for r = 9.5, 10, 11, 12, 15, 16, 18, 19 and short by the factor 2/pi for r = 2.5, 4, 5,
6, 8, 9, 13, 14, 17, 20, 22, 25. Every radius in this case was therefore taken from the first list, so
that its numbers would be the geometry and not a measurement artefact.
Since 2026-09-21 BSpline2D integrates the swept area of a rational spline instead of approximating it
(Gauss-Legendre with panel doubling), and every radius is exact. The radii here are left as they are -
they cost nothing and the case does not need rewriting - but a new case no longer has to avoid any.
Status:
Green from the day it was written, 2026-09-17. All four operations return, every volume meets its
calculated value to about 1e-8, and the shapes are the ones the Expected section predicts: coneMinusCyl
comes out as a ring with Euler 0 and one hole loop, cylMinusCone as two solids of 2974.04 and 2261.95.
Stable over 3 repeats.

The surfaces are what this case was written to see: RuledSurface for the ruled cone and
SurfaceOfLinearExtrusion for the extruded cylinder, in the operands and in every result. Nothing is
recognized as a ConicalSurface or a CylindricalSurface, which is correct for the current code - Make3D
builds a quadric only from a pair of Ellipse objects and there is no Ellipse anywhere in this case.
Should a later version recognize the quadric behind two rational circles, the 'surfaces' line is where
it shows up; that is a welcome improvement but one that has to be judged, not absorbed silently.

The companion tangential case on the same kind of surfaces is NurbsCylindersTangentAtSeam, which is
KnownFail. That the transversal one is green and the tangential one is not is the whole point of having
both: the ordinary intersection path on these surfaces works.
